title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Improves throughput and latency by introducing sequence-length aware dynamic batching with bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics. No API changes. Backwards-compatible runtime behavior. Rollout gated by canary flags.
description:
Context: continuous batching in the serving runtime reduces per-token cost but suffers when request sequence lengths are highly variable. Large padding overhead both increases compute and worsens tail latency. This PR introduces a sequence-length aware dynamic batching strategy: (1) bucketing by length ranges, (2) padding-minimization within buckets, and (3) an adaptive bucket reshaping heuristic driven by online request distribution. The goals are: reduce wasted tokens, improve end-to-end throughput, and keep p95/p99 latency stable for mixed workloads.

What changed (high level):
- Added a new Batcher module: seqlen_bucketed_batcher that groups inflight requests into buckets by sequence length ranges and emits minibatches that minimize internal padding.
- Implemented an adaptive bucket resizing policy: the runtime collects a lightweight histogram of recent request lengths and periodically rebuckets boundaries to match observed percentiles (configurable window size).
- Tight integration with KV cache: batching decisions now account for whether requests can reuse cached KV states (we prioritize co-batching requests that share KV warmness to avoid cache thrashing).
- Scheduler improvements: when generating batches across buckets we now allow cross-bucket merge only when the expected padding cost is below a configurable threshold; this prevents pathological merges that spike latency.
- Kernel selection hooks: the batcher exposes per-batch stats (max_seq, total_tokens) to the kernel selection layer so the runtime can choose optimized kernels for the batch shape (reduces inefficiency for extremely wide/narrow batches).
- Metrics and observability: new runtime metrics (batch.bucket_size, batch.padding_waste_tokens, batch.rebucket_events) and dashboard panels added in observability-pack for quick diagnosis.
- Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for bucket assignment, e2e perf harness updates, and canary benchmark scripts under perf-canary.

Why this approach:
- Static bucketing reduces padding at the cost of misaligned load as distributions drift. Adaptive bucketing provides a middle ground: we maintain low padding while remaining robust to distribution shifts. Combining bucket-aware scheduling and KV-awareness keeps both compute and cache locality high.

Performance (canary results):
- Mixed production-like workload (tokens/sec distribution from internal trace): throughput +18% on average, p95 latency -12%, p99 latency -6%, measured on a 4xA100 serving pool in the benchmark lab.
- Synthetic skewed-short workload: padding waste reduced by ~45%, TPU/GPU utilization improved correspondingly.
- Microbenchmarks: kernel-selection optimization reduced per-token wallclock by ~2-4% for long sequences.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default behavior: the feature is behind a runtime feature-flag (runtime.dynamic_batching.seqlen_bucketing) disabled by default for all tenants.
- Rollout steps: internal canary (perf-canary) -> 10% controlled rollout on dedicated -> scale to hosted API if metrics stable for 48h.
- Fallbacks: if padding_waste or p99 latency regresses beyond configured thresholds, the controller auto-disables the new batcher and reverts to previous continuous-batcher.

Files changed (high level):
- redwood/runtime/batcher/seqlen_bucketed_batcher.{cpp,h} - core algorithm and adaptive rebucketing logic.
- redwood/runtime/scheduler/scheduler.cpp - integration points and cross-bucket merge policy.
- redwood/runtime/kernel_selector/kernel_selector.cpp - added hints and selection paths for common batch shapes.
- redwood/runtime/kv_cache/kv_policy.cpp - KV-aware co-batching heuristics.
- perf-canary/benchmarks/dynamic_batching_bench.py - bench harness and workload configs.
- observability-pack/dashboards/batching_overview.json - dashboard with new metrics.
- tests/unit/test_seqlen_bucketed_batcher.cpp - unit and fuzz tests.

Commits (summary):
- Initial draft of seqlen_bucketed_batcher with static buckets and unit tests.
- Add adaptive rebucketing and histogram-based boundary computation.
- KV cache awareness and scheduler merge heuristics.
- Kernel selector hooks and minor perf improvements.
- Benchmarks, dashboards, and documentation.
- Fixes from review: increased histogram window, edge-case handling for single-request batches, and additional test coverage.

Review timeline and conversation (summary):
- Miguel Ortiz (review): asked for clarity on how rebucketing impacts in-flight batches and possible latency spikes during boundary changes. Requested a graceful rebucket transition to avoid mid-batch reshuffles.
- Author (Ava): implemented a two-phase rebucket where new boundaries apply only to newly accepted requests; in-flight batches continue with previous mapping. Added tests and noted the change in the description.
- Priya Nair (review): requested metrics for rebucket churn and suggested a lower default rebucket frequency; also asked to expose the feature-flag and thresholds via runtime config.
- Author: exposed runtime.dynamic_batching.* flags, added observability counters and lowered rebucket default to 5-minute window.
- Liam Patel (perf review): requested bench numbers with KV-warm and KV-cold mixes; found small regression in 1% tail on extreme long-sequence workloads and suggested limiting cross-bucket merges for batches where max_seq > 4x median.
- Author: implemented the extra merge threshold and re-ran canary; updated numbers in this description.

CI and checks: all CI checks passed after final fixes. Key CI items: clang-tidy, unit tests, integration/perf-canary smoke tests, and dashboard lint. One flaky unit test (test_batch_timeout_edge) failed initially and was fixed (race condition) in the follow-up commit.

Migration and configuration docs: added a short doc section in redwood-docs under runtime/batching.md explaining new flags, recommended thresholds, and how to interpret new metrics.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: misconfigured buckets could increase latency for rare long requests. Mitigation: conservative default bucket boundaries, rebucket cooldown, and automatic rollback thresholds.
- Risk: interaction with KV cache could cause cache-locality regression. Mitigation: KV-aware scoring prevents co-batching when it would reduce KV reuse.

Next steps:
- Monitor production canaries for two weeks and tune default bucket boundaries based on more traffic profiles.
- Explore ML-based boundary prediction for non-stationary traffic.
- Expose an admin API to suggest tenant-specific bucket profiles for large customers.

Notes: references to internal Linear tickets and benchmark harness included. This PR focuses on the runtime path and intentionally defers any SDK/API changes.
